Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a class-first resolution that uses Brightline’s complete member records to deliver relief without a claims barrier. Our opening term sheet is $36 million for the class, distributed automatically, plus $9 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline would not agree to clear sailing, and any fee amount not awarded by the court would be added to the class fund.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline is prepared to resolve this with automatic payments using its member records, but cannot meet the $45 million opening demand. We propose a $30 million class fund and $6 million in fees and expenses, with no clear-sailing commitment; any fee amount not approved by the court would be added to the class fund. This is a substantial, direct recovery for the class while keeping total cash outlay at $36 million.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s commitment to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fee amount to the class. We can make a substantial move from our opening position: $34 million for the class and $7 million in attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval, with no clear-sailing commitment and any unawarded fees added to the class fund. Automatic distribution remains essential given the complete member records.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We cannot accept a $41 million total outlay. To keep this class-first and ensure members receive relief automatically, Brightline proposes $33 million for the class and $6 million in fees and expenses. We retain no clear-sailing commitment, and any fees not awarded by the court would be added to the class fund. This is a $39 million total commitment.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline’s move to a $33 million automatic class fund is meaningful, and we appreciate keeping the no-clear-sailing and class-benefit treatment of any unawarded fees. To resolve the remaining gap, we propose a $34 million class fund with the same $6 million fee request and all other terms unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s movement and are prepared to narrow the remaining gap. We propose a $34 million class fund, with the $6 million fee request and all other terms unchanged: automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and any fees not awarded by the court added to the class fund. This is a limited final adjustment from our prior proposal and should resolve the remaining difference.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts Hargrove Lane LLP’s latest term sheet as binding, subject to court approval.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The parties negotiated over four rounds. Class counsel opened with a $36 million class fund and a $9 million fee-and-expense request; Brightline countered with a $30 million class fund and a $6 million fee-and-expense request. In subsequent rounds, counsel narrowed the dispute over the class fund while keeping automatic distribution, no clear-sailing commitment, and the provision directing any fee amount not awarded by the Court to the class. Brightline ultimately accepted class counsel’s proposal of a $34 million class fund and a $6 million fee-and-expense request, subject to Court approval. The settlement provides automatic payments using Brightline’s member records, avoiding a claims process. The negotiations were adversarial and involved movement by both sides.
